criteria: Deliver six initial courses: verifying identities and requests; protecting accounts and recovery methods; device, download and malicious-software risks; recognising manipulation in work and personal communications; verifying payments and signing requests; responding to suspected compromise. Each course contains lessons, a worked example, two interactive exercises with explanations and corrective feedback, and an assessment using unfamiliar examples. These are the initial courses, with later expansion supported by customer revenue.
All six courses are accessible in a test account, with saved progress.
All twelve exercises work, including plausible legitimate requests, not just obvious scams.
Thirty sourced case records support the teaching, each with its source, observation date and reviewed defensive guidance.
An independent reviewer checks every course and exercise against a published checklist. Critical factual errors or unsafe guidance must be corrected before acceptance.
Publish an inventory identifying the new work and excluding previously funded work.
milestones.name: Six complete courses, ready for independent testing

criteria: Deliver the hosted product connecting courses, assessments and case guidance. The independent reviewer demonstrates that an individual can join, purchase access, take courses, resume progress and complete an assessment.
The independent reviewer demonstrates that a team manager can assign training and see completion records, while private case submissions remain inaccessible to the manager.
The independent reviewer demonstrates that a new account receives exactly three free case checks, followed by the published paid allowance.
The independent reviewer demonstrates that a case answer explains relevant warning signs, missing information, verification steps and related training.
The independent reviewer demonstrates that users can delete their case submissions, and one account cannot retrieve another account's private cases.

Test the assistant using 80 independently reviewed examples: 30 scams, 30 legitimate requests and 20 situations with insufficient evidence. At least 90% must meet the agreed answer rubric, with no critical unsafe recommendations. Uncertain cases must not receive an unsupported safe verdict.
Publish the test method, results and remaining limitations without exposing private submissions.
milestones.name: Working paid platform and case assistant

criteria: 500 distinct outside Ethereum/L2 learners have paid for access, personally or through their employer, and completed all six initial courses and their assessments. Each assessment requires at least 80%, with every designated critical protective action correct. Exclude staff, test accounts, duplicates, refunded purchases and grant-funded seats. One person counts once, regardless of how many courses they complete.
At least 10 Ethereum organizations pay for team access, 3 of them with over $50 million TVL onchain or over a $100M market cap on their token.

For three consecutive calendar months, earned customer revenue minus payment fees, refunds, hosting, AI usage, delivery, support, content maintenance and ongoing labour costs is greater than zero. Count founder and contractor operating time at rates disclosed in advance. Exclude grant income and recognise annual subscriptions over the service period rather than counting the entire payment immediately.
milestones.name: 500 paying learners complete training, with three months of operating profitability

sections.commitments:
- Maintain funded materials and essential corrections for twelve months from release. Customer revenue supports continuing operation and curriculum expansion.
- Publish new rights-cleared teaching handouts and assessment criteria under CC BY 4.0. Existing software and third-party material retain their licences.
- Preserve existing free and member rights. Protect private case inputs.
- Define the required core learning path and assessment rules before recruitment. Count distinct people, not course registrations or video views.
sections.in_scope:
**Multiple practical courses.** The initial library covers identity verification, account and device security, suspicious software requests, payments and signing, and incident response. It includes 30 reviewed case records and 12 practical exercises, with legitimate counterparts, explanations, corrective feedback and fresh assessments. The curriculum can grow as threats and learner needs change.

**A case assistant connected to training.** Users describe or paste a suspicious message or situation. The assistant explains supported warning signs, identifies missing information, suggests protective steps and recommends relevant lessons. It makes uncertainty explicit and does not declare something safe merely because it finds no known scam pattern.

**One paid subscription.** Access includes the standard paid course library, updates and a bounded assistant allowance. Individuals receive three free checks. Team access adds training assignment and completion records.

**Free educational resources.** Provide videos with Carlos's narration and Zealynx explanatory cards. Reviewed research also supports course updates, case guidance and newsletter material, with source dates and human review before publication.

The proposed fifteen-month schedule is approximately three months for the initial release, followed by twelve months to demonstrate paid adoption and sustainable operation.
sections.out_scope: Audits, guaranteed scam detection, automatic replies or transactions, continuous inbox monitoring, unlimited coaching and payment for completed work.
sections.team:
Carlos Vendrell leads Zealynx's security work and Academy. Zealynx owns the platform and delivers the programme.

Earlier Academy support was 6.4466 ETH, valued at $12,008 when sent in [TheDAO's transparency record](https://thedao.fund/transparency/). Completed and previously funded work is excluded from this request.
sections.why:
Ethereum security depends on the people controlling accounts, devices, software and signing permissions. Convincing messages, impersonation and malicious requests can persuade someone to bypass otherwise sound protections. The [FBI documents targeted social engineering against crypto employees](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA240903).

People need practical ways to verify requests, recognise uncertainty and respond safely. Zealynx Defence connects structured training with guidance when a suspicious situation actually happens. Learners practise decisions and demonstrate understanding on unfamiliar examples. Completion shows the skills assessed; it does not guarantee immunity from deception.
sections.why_grant:
Academy Defence already provides simulated security drills. Zealynx also has sourced research on scams and attacks to inform the programme.

Reusing this foundation reduces development work. The grant funds the additional curriculum, assessment, reviewed case guidance and software needed to deliver a paid training service.

initiative.summary: Build a paid training platform that helps Ethereum teams recognise deception, verify suspicious requests and practise safer decisions. One subscription includes an expanding course library and a case assistant that explains suspicious situations, suggests verification steps and recommends relevant training. Three free checks introduce the tool. TheDAO supports creation; customer subscriptions sustain delivery and updates.
initiative.title: Zealynx Defence: practical security training and help with suspicious messages
